name: bufwrite
algorithm: Write n lines "<i> <i*0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 in hex> <i*7>" to a file in the temporary directory through each language's std formatter and a 64 KiB buffered writer, then read the file back; its length plus FNV-1a 64 of its bytes, wrapping (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the hex value and the checksum already use the wrapping operators; i*7 cannot overflow at these sizes

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; every column writes the same bytes, and the checksum over the bytes read back checks the formatter and the writer
notes: Formatters and writers named: mk Print through fs.File.Writer (64 KiB); c fprintf on a stream with setvbuf _IOFBF 65536; rust writeln! through BufWriter::with_capacity(65536); zig print through File.writer over 64 KiB; go fmt.Fprintf through bufio.NewWriterSize(65536); cs Utf8.TryWrite through FileStream (65536 buffer). Every column goes through its general formatter (critic F26).
Each column writes its own file name in its temporary directory (TMP on Windows) and removes it; the file is at most 102 MB at the publish size (34 bytes a line at most).
